newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-A third of Australian budget bill lost - Labor.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-A third of Australian budget bill lost - Labor.

text.p: The Australian Senate amended one of the government's budget bills on Tuesday and the Labor opposition estimated that the amendments would cost about a third of the bill's savings, which were to exceed A$140 million a year or more.
The Social Security (Newly Arrived Resident's Waiting Periods) Bill was amended to defeat part of the government's plan to exclude immigrants from social security for two years after their arrival.
The Senate left untouched the exclusion from unemployment benefits but abolished the attempt to exclude immigrants from other social security.
"We reckon it takes about a third," a Labor spokeswoman said.
The August 20 budget estimated the waiting-periods measure was worth A$140 million in the fiscal year to June 1998, rising to A$193 million in 1999/00.
